fig1.one_point: one (matrix, singular index) pair; 72 matrices at the step-2528 checkpoint; the tail column is each matrix's median response over directions with singular value below 0.1 of its largest
fig1.takeaway: the deployed 12-iteration Newton-Schulz reproduces the exact polar factor at every resolved singular index; suppression exists only in the small-singular tail and only below 8 iterations

fig2.one_point: one (matrix, singular index) pair at the step-2528 checkpoint; 12 matrices per panel (one per block)
fig2.takeaway: the momentum's four leading singular directions all oscillate at period two, and curvature falls roughly sixfold from the first to the second singular direction; the polar factor then assigns all of them equal step size

fig3.one_point: one line = one matrix at the step-2528 checkpoint (record kernel; 12 lines per panel per basis)
fig3.takeaway: the activation preconditioner cuts curvature along the realized update to roughly 60 percent at alpha 0.5; replacing its eigenbasis with a random one (same eigenvalues) removes most of the effect, so the value is carried by the basis

fig4.one_point: left: one (matrix, checkpoint), 216 points, diagonal = identical Newton effect under both momenta; right: one matrix at step 2528, diagonal = rotation independent of basis choice
fig4.takeaway: the preconditioner's curvature effect is the same whichever momentum it acts on, and how far it rotates the update is set by its eigenvalue spread alone -- rotation does not measure Newton content

fig5.one_point: left: one (matrix, singular index) from 32 consecutive 8192-token microbatches drawn from the training stream at a frozen checkpoint, three checkpoints overlaid; right: one line = one matrix (leading direction) across microbatch sizes at step 2528, two sizes at step 3028
fig5.takeaway: the leading direction's signal-to-noise ratio collapses across training (about 6 to 2 to 0.4) and grows sublinearly with tokens (log-log slope about 0.55, below the slope-1 line that independent tokens would give); microbatches are consecutive stream chunks, so the cross-size slope is the robust readout and the noise a batch delivers must be measured, not derived from batch size
